body_markdown:
Like other New Yorkers, you’re likely utilizing the city’s public transportation on a daily basis to get around New York City. One of these options includes the subway system, which runs through the different parts of the city, from the Bronx, Manhattan, Queens, to Brooklyn. Folks who need to commute daily to work will often choose to live in a neighborhood that has an NYC subway stop that directly connects to work. During the last few months, we spent time going over the various train routes and neighborhoods along those particular subway lines and covered the W train route in our last article. Today, we’re moving on to the S train shuttle routes which run in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn. We’ll go over each of the subway stations the S train stops at and discuss the best neighborhoods to live in on its route.


# S train stops NYC


Compared to other train routes, the S train runs on three separate shuttle routes in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens. Each route is quite short. The Manhattan route only has two stops, the Brooklyn route has 4 stops, and the Queens route has 5 total stops. The shuttle route in Manhattan runs on 42nd Street between Times Square and Grand Central and runs horizontally to bring commuters from one side of Manhattan to the other. The shuttle route in Brooklyn vertically between Franklin Ave and Prospect Park. This shuttle line runs above ground. Finally, the shuttle route in Queens runs between the Broad Channel and the southern part of the Rockaway peninsula. This shuttle largely overlaps with the A train but is an important service for locals and beachgoers alike.


In order from Manhattan, Brooklyn, to Queens is a list of stops that the S train stops at. We’ve specifically pointed out stops that service the S train. For your convenience, we’ve also marked the stops that are ADA accessible.


### Manhattan stops:


- Times Sq-42 St (Express) (ADA Accessible) (Terminal) – also services N, Q, R, W, 1, 2, 3, 7, A, C, and E route


- Grand Central-42 St (Express) (ADA Accessible) (Terminal) – also services 4, 5, 6, 7 route


### Brooklyn stops:


- Franklin Av (Local) – also services A, C route


- Park Place (Local) (ADA Accessible)


- Botanic Garden (Local) – also services 2, 3, 4, 5 route


- Prospect Park (Local and Express) (ADA Accessible) – also services Q, B route


### Queens stops:


- Broad Channel (Local) – also services A route


- Beach 90 St (Local) – also services A route


- Beach 98 St (Local) – also services A route


- Beach 105 St (Local) – also services A route


- Rockaway Park-Beach 116 St (Local) (ADA Accessible) – also services A route


You can also locate an


[S train stops map in PDF format](https://www.mta.info/map/5341) directly on the MTA’s site. Alternatively, you can read through a


[text format of the S train stops map here](https://www.mta.info/maps/subway-line-maps/s-line) .


## Best Manhattan neighborhoods along S train stops


### Midtown East


The neighborhood


[Midtown East](https://www.renthop.com/apartments-for-rent/midtown-east-new-york-ny) is located on the east side of the S train stop at Grand Central. This neighborhood is quite large, stretching from 42nd Street to 59th Street and from 5th Avenue all the way to the water. The area is popular with folks who work in Midtown, but there are also plenty who commute to other parts of the city such as northern and southern Manhattan, or to Queens and Brooklyn. Residents of the neighborhood have easy access to plenty of restaurants, bars, and cafes.


## Best Brooklyn neighborhoods along S train stops


### Crown Heights


The S train route in Brooklyn runs through the neighborhood of


[Crown Heights](https://www.renthop.com/apartments-for-rent/crown-heights-new-york-ny) . This relatively large neighborhood is located in Central Brooklyn and is bordered by Prospect Heights to the west, Flatbush, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and East Flatbush to the south, Brownsville to the east, and Bedford-Stuyvesant to the north. The neighborhood is cut in half by the Eastern Pkwy running through it and has a few major commercial-heavy streets, such as Franklin Ave, Norstrand Ave, Kingston Ave, and Utica Ave. Residents of the neighborhood have easy access to Prospect Park, including the zoo and the botanical garden.


## Best Queens neighborhoods along S train stops


### Rockaway Park


The neighborhood of


[Rockaway Park](https://www.renthop.com/search?areas=rockaway-beach-new-york-ny) is located on the Rockaway Peninsula in Queens. The neighborhood runs between Beach 126th Street and Beach 109th Street. About 50% of the neighborhood is residential. However, given its proximity to the Rockaway Beach, there are a large number of businesses along the boardwalk on the south side of the neighborhood and along Beach 116th Street and Rockaway Beach Blvd. Residents may have a longer commute to the rest of the city, however, they have easy access to the beaches along the peninsula.
